Standard: Corrosion capability of static and rotating parts is such that the engine capability established in 7.2 standards is not adversely affected, engine operating limits are not exceeded, and detrimental permanent deformation or damage does not occur when the engine is operated, under steady state and transient conditions, IAW 7.3.1 for the stated life documented in engine technical data. Corrosion capability includes all forms of environmental attack (e.g., stress corrosion cracking, hot corrosion, sulfidation, intergranular corrosion). Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examine CPCP that describes activities throughout the life cycle to establish and maintain corrosion resistance of engine hardware to ensure content is consistent with MIL-STD-1568, General Requirements and CPCP paragraphs. Analysis.
  (1) Review analysis of the materials, coatings, and material interfaces (material pairs) used in the engine to ensure they are not corrosion prone or corrosion sensitive and that corrosion protective measures are effective. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (1) Lab test: Substantiate corrosion resistance and effects through engine testing in a sea-level test cell with a corrosive environment as defined in JSSG-2007, Appendix A, Verification section, Corrosive Atmosphere paragraph. Turboshaft engine corrosion susceptibility test is preceded by two hours of sand ingestion if design usage includes significant time in sand and dust environments.
